doc.title: Jerry Jerome interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Opening, Sarasota, and Jerry's papers in archives
summary: Monk Rowe opens the filmed interview; Jerry says he has lived in Sarasota 23 years, was raised in New Jersey and lived on Long Island, and gave material to the Museum of Broadcasting and the New School.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive, here in Sarasota, and it’s my great pleasure to have saxophonist and arranger Jerry Jerome. Welcome.
Thank you, Monk. It’s good to be here.
It’s great to be down here.
We did. And we are hearing some great music at the festival. And you are a long time resident of this area, I guess we could say long time now.
Originally raised in New Jersey, and my whole married life, professional life, was centered around New York and Long Island. I lived on Long Island, in Roslyn.
You know I read that the University of Wyoming has some of your music in their archive, is that right?
I think I read something about that.
If it’s true we’re jealous, and we want some too.

Well sure, be happy to. I don’t recall. When I broke the house down on Long Island I gave a lot of my material to the Museum of Broadcasting in New York and the New School. But I think Dick Hyman’s wife spoke to me about Wyoming, I might have.
I’ll just show you where I read that, maybe it’s true. Did you start out as a clarinetist?
